title: Harnessing bound states in the continuum for quantum and nonlinear photonics in silicon nitride microresonators
authors: Eduardo C. Lima, Marco Clementi, Alice Viola, Matteo Galli, Daniele Bajoni, Marco Liscidini, Massimo Borghi
abstract: In this work we theoretically and experimentally investigate bound states in the continuum (BICs) in a reconfigurable integrated photonic structure, focusing on spontaneous four-wave mixing. We consider a configuration in which only one mode, the idler, is tuned to the BIC condition, and show that suppressing the radiative loss of this single mode profoundly reshapes the overall nonlinear dynamics. In particularly, we realize electrically tunable Friedrich-Wintgen BICs with Q > 10^6 in an interferometrically coupled silicon-nitride microresonator. Although inaccessible through linear excitation, the BIC is populated by four-wave mixing and read out through its radiative photon partner. In the low-gain regime, we investigate the spectral, correlation, and coherence properties of the generated photon pairs, revealing distinctive signatures in the signal-idler correlations and an extracted signal whose coherence time approaches the intrinsic-loss-limited lifetime of the dark idler. In the high-gain regime, making one mode participating in optical parametric amplification a BIC enhances the parametric gain by 12 dB and lowers the oscillation threshold by 1.6 dB. These results establish BICs as a tool for mode-selective lifetime engineering, enabling control over both biphoton wavepackets and the threshold dynamics of integrated parametric devices.
summary: This paper explores using Bound States in the Continuum (BICs) within silicon nitride microresonators to control nonlinear photonics. By tuning one mode into a BIC state, researchers can profoundly alter spontaneous four-wave mixing and parametric amplification processes. This technique establishes BICs as a method for precise 'mode-selective lifetime engineering' of integrated optical devices.
main_problem: The work investigates utilizing Bound States in the Continuum (BICs) within integrated photonic structures to fundamentally reshape nonlinear optical dynamics, particularly through spontaneous four-wave mixing and parametric amplification.
main_result: Achieving BIC conditions allows for mode-selective lifetime engineering, enhancing parametric gain by 12 dB and lowering the oscillation threshold by 1.6 dB compared to standard resonances.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling (extending field quantization to include discrete BIC modes) with experimental characterization of nonlinear processes like SFWM and OPA in silicon nitride microresonators.
model_or_system: The physical system is a reconfigurable integrated photonic structure using silicon nitride microresonators, featuring an asymmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer coupled to a bus waveguide. BICs are realized by tuning the coupling such that one mode becomes decoupled from the continuum modes.
key_observables: Signal-idler correlations in photon pairs, parametric gain enhancement (up to 12 dB), and reduction of oscillation threshold (by 1.6 dB).
important_parameters: High Quality Factor ($Q > 10^6$), low/high-gain regimes for nonlinear processes, and the ability to tune coupling coefficients via auxiliary resonators.
main_assumptions: The theoretical framework assumes orthogonality between BIC and asymptotic fields; experimentally, precise tuning of coupling is required to achieve near-zero radiative loss.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate mode solutions (propagating vs. confined BIC), the device structure showing how an auxiliary resonator creates BICs, and comparative plots demonstrating OPA gain in both BIC and standard resonance configurations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework for incorporating discrete BIC modes into nonlinear Hamiltonians, to experimentally validating the selective creation of these BICs by tuning coupling, and finally applying this control to enhance parametric amplification processes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it demonstrates a powerful tool—BICs—for engineering the decay rates and interaction strengths in open quantum optical systems, directly impacting nonlinear light-matter interactions.
